rule: Git preserves durable receipts (locator, class, byte length, SHA-256) and no raw third-party bytes are promoted into Git. Audio, archived HTML and ASR derivatives are re-acquirable from the recorded locators; a full SHA-256 proves which bytes were acquired on this pass. Machine transcription (ASR) is a locating derivative only and is never the wording authority. PUBLICATION_HOLD is independent of custody completeness.

pageStateObservations.observation: Pass 8 (early-life lane, file 28_): two dated public retellings of the Dauphin Way exit are now documented - the Shepherds' Conference 2006 GS7 Q&A (03.03.2006) eyewitness account by Fred Butler (Hip and Thigh, full text via Wayback snapshot 20160604044239: 'kicked him out of the Church for being Calvinistic') and the SC2007 GS8 Q&A lead; the SC2006 GS7 MP3 byte locator is established from the open S3 listing (md5 ef39c0a214a09ea78e843c53debd738e, 15,594,935 bytes). Lawson's own full BGEA account (The Cripplegate, 22.02.2018) is obtained, with external corroboration of the September 1989 Little Rock crusade (War Memorial Stadium, seven nights) but not of his personal role; the RTS D.Min. dissertation is absent from TREN (0 hits for the exact author). Internet Archive inside-search for Men Who Win (1992) is closed on every tested route (private derivatives; archivelab HTTP 500; fulltext endpoint 'item not available'; Open Library captcha). Correction recorded: Butler's 'weeping' passage refers to S. Lewis Johnson, not to the Dauphin Way recounting.

gracechurch.org 2017 Shepherds' Conference catalogue lists General Sessions 1–13 and 15 but not Session 14, and does not list Lawson's seminar session; Wayback captures 20241203112858 and 20250317203624 show the same state; the official Session 14 MP3 remains reachable.
All five ligonier.org pages for the 2023 London conference featuring Lawson return HTTP 404; non-Lawson session pages return 200.

Official Ligonier YouTube playlist for the 2023 London conference (13 items) retains Lawson's Q&A/panel appearances but omits both of his solo sessions («The Word of God for Exiles»; «Preach the Word»); the corresponding ligonier.org pages return 404.

SermonAudio catalogue shows a broadcast titled The Word of God for Exiles (Sermon ID 10122311204054; 44:28; card date 2023-10-11; Category: Conference; Bible Text 1 Peter 1:23; 2 Timothy 3:16-17; Broadcaster Grace Audio Treasures; Series Puritan Devotional) whose duration is identical to the third-party YouTube re-upload Ey7kYHEpcyo (2668 s). Media host returned 502 at capture; identity of the recordings is NOT asserted.

Audio for the SermonAudio broadcast of The Word of God for Exiles was obtained later on 2026-09-27 (32 173 613 B; 2668.16 s; ID3 album Grace Audio Treasures, comment Puritan Devotional). Four sampled windows transcribe to the same text as the auto-captions of the YouTube re-upload Ey7kYHEpcyo, including the Word of God possesses the right to bind our conscience (14:09). Identity of the two third-party copies is verified; the official Ligonier object remains absent.

On 2026-09-27 evening the Internet Archive web endpoints returned 'Internet Archive: Temporarily Offline' (HTTP 503) for onepassion.org CDX queries and an empty CDX result for trinitybiblechurchofdallas.com; archive.today was unreachable (HTTP 000) from the sandbox; Google Books API returned HTTP 429; OpenLibrary has no record of the book. These are infrastructure/search negatives, not evidence of absence.

Ligonier's official conference programme pages confirm both 2023 London sessions by Lawson (pre-conference 'Preach the Word'; main 'The Word of God for Exiles', Westminster Chapel, 8-9 September 2023), but no official media objects were located; the former event page returns HTTP 404.

The published sample pages of Mercy in the Wilderness (as reproduced by Protestia on 2026-09-21) are now in custody with hashes; they carry verbatim self-description but no page numbers, so book quotations remain limited to 'released sample pages' framing.

On 2026-09-27 the Internet Archive came back online for URL-level queries. Wayback holds at least eight mementos of the X statement URL (first capture 2025-03-14, two days after posting), but the March captures are JavaScript shells containing no statement text; captures of 2025-07-06 and 2025-08-16 return X's own page-does-not-exist view. No conclusion about who removed the post is drawn; the durable wording remains via outlet carriers.

The Trinity September 2024 statement text was reconstructed sentence by sentence from six carriers. Sentences 5-8 (Christ remains Head of the church; the Lord was building Trinity long before and after Steve Lawson; the 1 Cor 10:12 appeal) were absent from the corpus before this pass. The original church page object is still missing; the church domain has only a 2019 Wayback snapshot.
OnePassion's public statement page was still published on 2025-01-23 (second memento), i.e., the institutional text persisted for months, unlike the personal X post.

The Trinity September 2024 statement was located as an archived capture of the church homepage (2024-09-19 17:01 UTC). The statement block is byte-identical across four captures through 2024-10-01 (no edits). The full text contains two sentences absent from all news carriers: the ministry start date January 5, 2018, and the primacy-of-exposition sentence about various men filling the pulpit each week. The pre-fall capture of 2024-09-14 lists Lawson's 8 September 2024 sermon as the latest and carries no announcement.

On 2026-09-27 X's public oEmbed service returned 404 for both the statement post and the @DrStevenJLawson handle while returning 200 for control tweets/accounts. The account and post are not publicly retrievable via that service; no claim is made about who removed them or when. The text of the statement remains documented through outlet carriers and the archived church page.

The OnePassion podcast feed (feeds.simplecast.com/XFCLnrvQ) returns 404; third-party catalogues list the last episode as 2024-09-12 with status Idle. Romans-series episodes survive on third-party platforms as locators, not as citation objects.

The Trinity Leadership page listed Dr. Steven J. Lawson as Lead Preacher (distinct from the elders) on 2024-08-14; his entry was gone in the capture of 2024-09-19 17:01 UTC, the same moment the statement appeared, with elders and deacons unchanged. The homepage ANNOUNCEMENT block remained present in captures from 2024-09-19 through 2024-10-08 (last known present: 2024-10-08 20:38 UTC) and was gone by 2024-10-15 03:19 UTC - removed between 8 and 15 October 2024. Recorded as page states; no motive inferred.

A public dispute over Lawson's membership at Trinity Bible Church ran through November 2024: the With All Wisdom podcast asserted he was neither pastor, elder nor (formally) a member, citing a staff member and church members; G3 Ministries stated that the facts are clear and that Lawson and his wife are members, citing two sources inside the church. Trinity itself never publicly addressed membership or discipline. The corpus now records both sides with verbatim quotes, publication rules requiring both positions, and the 2025-05-12 G3 statement about its then-president as context about the author of side B, explicitly not as evidence on the merits.

Pass 2 (book, conference, current status): the September 2026 wave around *Mercy in the Wilderness* is fully recorded (metadata with But God Press/print-on-demand; one substantive review whose book quotes stay carrier-bound; volatile Amazon rating excluded from publication). The July 2026 Contending for the Faith episode is established by three independent carriers plus the organizers' statement: he was invited, advertised without his consent, declined, and was removed (26 to 24) - the correct wording is 'invited, declined', never 'tried to return'. The 2026 status (Nashville, Stephens Valley Church, no leadership role) is recorded as reported. The official GTY 70-58 transcript adds paragraph-level locators and a new binding boundary: 'unfaithful leaders are being exposed' is a general statement in a passage naming other cases, not a personal label for Lawson. Two publication hazards are now explicit: the Christian Post misidentification of the correspondent Casey Staats as the woman, and the two 'Steven J. Lawson' author profiles on Amazon. No official Ligonier statement exists; the action is carried by MinistryWatch only. Russian-language material (including the VK article lead) remains unfound.

Pass 3 (institutional trail): the organizations' own pages now document the response in dated steps. Ligonier kept its teacher page but (a) stripped his titles between 16 and 23 Sep 2024 (teaching fellow; professor of preaching and dean of D.Min. at TMS; teacher for the Institute for Expository Preaching; author list) and (b) added between 27 Sep and 9 Oct 2024 the notice 'His content is no longer featured due to violations of our content policy' - which remains on the live page today with '0 Results'. That notice is the first official Ligonier object in the case and closes the open P1 item previously carried only by MinistryWatch. The Master's Seminary faculty page moved from 200 (last capture 10 Jul 2024) to 404 (captures from 20 Sep 2024) and stays 404, with no Lawson in the faculty index; Reformation Bible College's 'Visiting Professor' page is gone (last 200 capture 11 Sep 2024; live 404); Shepherds Conference listed him in the SC2024 speakers page and no longer lists him by Jan 2025 or today. OnePassion's site currently fails to serve on our routes (TLS handshake failure, Cloudflare 409, no homepage captures after January 2025) - recorded as an infrastructure observation with an explicit caveat and no inference. All changes are recorded as dated windows with no motive claims, and the Ligonier wording must never be expanded into a specification of what the violations were.

Pass 4 (accountability and ecclesiology): the Side A podcast was not one episode but a seven-episode series (#96-#102, 21 Oct - 27 Nov 2024) per its own RSS feed, and its central claims are now verified verbatim from its own audio with timecodes ('he was not a pastor. He was not an elder... He was not a member of that church' ~704-714s; 'kind of waffled when I said, was he a member' ~735-740s; 'the elders... are not the ones managing the Matthew 18 process... because they can't' ~741-754s), which upgrades these from a Protestia retelling to Side A's own primary publication while leaving them contested (the only source is an unnamed staff member). Episode #102 adds a coherent ecclesiological argument: the guest-preacher model itself is treated as partly responsible, with 'dynamic guest preachers' quoted from Trinity's own 'what to expect' page as of late Nov 2024. Side A's interpretation 'lead guest preacher' and 'Trinity admits we can't do anything' are marked as their characterisations, never as church statements. The Roys Report (24 Jan 2025) adds a third voice to the membership dispute: Stephens Valley pastor Jim Bachmann says Lawson attends SVC (where his brother is a member), is not an SVC member so SVC cannot discipline him, meets two professional counselors and elders regularly, moved to give his wife space and visited her in Dallas in January; and Bachmann believes Lawson was and still is a member of Trinity and is not under Trinity's discipline, with no contact from Trinity leadership and no response to TRR's request. Recorded as one pastor's attributed opinion, not a resolution. Full MP3s were deleted after transcription to respect workspace limits; hashes, sizes and URLs are recorded.

Pass 5 (series completion): episodes #96, #97 and #101 of the With All Wisdom series were acquired and transcribed, completing the primary-audio coverage of the Side A chronology. Two findings matter for discipline. First, on 21 Oct 2024 (#96) the membership claim was still attributed to others ('some have verified... some have said that he was not even a member of the church'), while the hosts' own assertion dates from 4 Nov 2024 (#98) after contact with a staff member - so the corpus must not date Side A's assertion earlier than 4 Nov. Second, episode #101 (25 Nov 2024) documents from Side A's own mouth the exact sequence the corpus previously held only through documents: their report, 'exactly 10 days later' the G3 counter-statement, their brief response citing a staff member, and 'eight days' later still no public answer from Trinity; it also records their formal-vs-default membership distinction and their 'we are not upset at G3' statement. Episode #96 confirms the allegation details (five years, late twenties, father confronted, 'no literal fornication') are sourced to Phil Johnson's X posts, which the corpus already attributes that way. The Christian Research Institute's Viewpoint article (Christian Research Journal 47:4, 2 Oct 2024, updated 2026) is added as external editorial support for terminology discipline, explicitly not as evidence about Lawson.

Corpus consolidation pass: the canonical Russian draft was advanced to v4 (file 17_) absorbing all five passes, the evidence dossier 01 gained a dated pass index, and a full cross-corpus reconciliation (file 18_) fixed the publication base and recorded four publication-safety defects in the parallel VK article: membership asserted as fact (the church never publicly said it), an unattributed 'permanently disqualified' attribution, a translated book title presented as if it were the book's title, and review-dependent claims that must keep their attribution. Seven items from the VK article (the August-September 2024 sermon sequence, Clint Archer's account, the Benzinger testimony, two Lawson quotes, Mohler/Piper/9Marks/Carson material, the favorable review, and the March 2025 accountability wording) are recorded as leads to migrate only after their own objects are obtained. No previously held claim, quote or rule was weakened; editorial history (03 -> 05 -> 07 -> 17) is preserved.
